global: Let the chroniclers record that {player} has laid siege to {fief}. Let them also record how it ends for the besiegers.
The gates of {fief} are shut and its walls are manned. Whoever comes to test them will learn what our fathers already knew.
Ser {player} thinks a ring of tents will break us. Our bread is baked and our wells are full. Let them sit in the mud.
Mark it well: the siege of {fief} will be sung of, though not in the way the besiegers hope.
Lay down your banners and go home, ser {player}. This hill has seen better armies than yours, and they are dust now.
Shame on the dogs who march against {fief} with fire in their hands. Honour has no place in such a camp.
I do not fear a siege from one who fights like a farmer's son. {fief} has stood for ages and it will stand for ages more.
Ser {player} lingers before our walls with nothing but patience. Patience is a poor weapon against stone and oath.
whisper: Ser {player}, you have made an enemy of every soul within {fief}. I shall remember the name you chose to besiege us with.
Your camp smells of fear and your ditches are shallow. Dig deeper if you mean to stay, friend, for you will need the depth.
I will not parley with you under a banner I do not recognise. Come back when you carry an honest flag, ser {player}.
Every arrow we loose at your tents is a debt you have incurred. I keep a long ledger, and yours is growing fast.
A siege is a slow death for the besieger too. Ask yourself whether your men will still stand beside you by the new moon.
You mistake my silence for weakness, ser {player}. The stones of {fief} have heard bolder men than you and kept their silence.
Withdraw from {fief} while you still have men to lead home, or I will make sure your name is spoken only as a warning.
Your sons will ask why you chose a wall of stone over a quiet hearth, ser {player}. I wonder what you will answer them.

global: A siege has begun at {fief}. I take no side in it yet, but I shall watch how the banners fall before I make my choice.
Word reaches the road that {player} has encamped before {fief}. Travellers should give the valley a wide berth until matters settle.
The tents below {fief} are a sorry sight to a weary rider. May both sides find their wits before the winter rains come.
Let no man say I am eager to take part in the quarrel before {fief}. My horse needs rest and my purse needs mending.
Whether {player} has right on their side or only ambition, the siege of {fief} will test them. We shall see which.
Grain carts have stopped on the road to {fief}. Merchants are nervous, and so am I, for a hungry town makes hasty friends.
Ser {player} has chosen a long quarrel. I have seen such quarrels end in ruin for all, and I pray this one is different.
I hear the horns of {fief} sounding the alarm. Pass me the wine and tell me when the gates open, or when the army retreats.
whisper: Ser {player}, I bear no grudge against you yet, but I would know your purpose before I speak of {fief} to anyone else.
My sympathies are divided, friend. Explain why you have come to {fief} with an army, and I shall consider the matter fairly.
I will not lend coin or men to your cause at {fief}, ser {player}, but neither will I raise my voice against it. Good fortune.
Tread carefully before {fief}. Its lord is patient and its captains are stubborn, and a patient enemy is a dangerous one.
Your siege has drawn eyes from every hall on this road, ser {player}. Consider who among them might prefer you to fail.
I have no quarrel with you, friend, but I have an interest in how the siege of {fief} ends. Send word when it does.
Should you need a safe road away from {fief}, I can point one out. I offer it as a courtesy and nothing more, ser {player}.
Keep your banners low while the town watches, ser {player}. A show of colours can make enemies of neighbours who had none.
